title: Space and the planets for kids
examples: What is the difference between a star and a planet?
How far away is the Moon from Earth?
Are all the planets the same size?

explain.say: The Sun is a giant star. It gives us light and heat.

draw.text: Space and the planets for kids

explain.say: Now look. This is the solar system in 3D. Can you see the Sun and Mercury? Tap any part to hear about it.

draw.text: Space and the planets for kids

explain.say: Eight planets go around the Sun. They are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.
The Moon goes around the Earth. It makes no light of its own. It reflects the Sun's light.
Stars are huge balls of very hot gas, like the Sun. They are very far away.

items: Stars are giant balls of gas

explain.say: Watch the Moon on different nights. It follows a path around the Earth.
At night, you can see many stars. They twinkle because the Earth's air moves.

faq.q: Why is the Sun so important to us?
faq.a: The Sun provides the light that lets us see during the day. It also gives us the heat that keeps Earth warm enough for life.
asks: What does the Sun give off?
Is the Sun like a giant lamp?

faq.q: Does the Moon make any light?
faq.a: No, the Moon does not make its own light. It only shines because it bounces the light from the Sun back to our eyes.
asks: Where does the Moon get its light?
Can the Moon shine at night?

faq.q: Are all the planets the same size?
faq.a: No, the planets are very different sizes. Jupiter is much bigger than Earth, for example.
asks: Are all planets the same size?

faq.q: What is the difference between a star and a planet?
faq.a: A star, like the Sun, makes its own light and heat. A planet, like Earth, goes around a star and makes no light.
asks: What is the main difference between stars and planets?

faq.a: The solar system is the Sun and everything that goes around it, like the planets and their moons.
asks: What is everything in space called?
What makes up our solar system?

facts: The Sun is a star, not a planet.
The eight planets orbit the Sun in order.
Stars shine because they produce their own energy.

quiz.say: Which one is a star that makes its own light?
quiz.show: Which one makes its own light?
quiz.why: The Sun is a star. Stars make their own light and heat.

wrong.0: The Moon reflects sunlight, and makes no light of its own.
wrong.1: The Earth is a planet, and it makes no light.

quiz.say: What does the Moon go around?
quiz.why: The Moon goes around the Earth about once a month.

wrong.1: Mars has its own small moons.
wrong.2: The stars are far away, much farther than the Moon.

quiz.say: How many planets go around the Sun?
quiz.why: There are eight planets, from Mercury to Neptune.

wrong.0: Pluto used to be counted, but now it is called a dwarf planet.
wrong.2: Seven is one too few, so count again from Mercury to Neptune.
